T0613: What it does: in a finished puzzle, count the walls that touch the outline (1 each), the corners where 3 walls meet, a T (1 each), and where 4 meet, a cross (2 each). On a board in one piece without holes the total is always exactly 2 x (pieces - 1). When the rules cap the number of pieces, the walls have a budget: an edge whose wall would go over it is a link. Example: 16 tiles with Precision 4 = 4 pieces, budget 6; two walls from border to border use 4, a T uses 1, so a wall that would cost 2 more is impossible.
T0616: What it does: only when Match leaves exactly two pieces, inside the final search. One piece is the other one turned, flipped and moved; the solver tries each possible move, and for that move every edge and its copy must be the same (wall to wall, link to link). A known edge gives its copy.
T0617: What it does: see T0616. The current text is vague; something closer: 'With only two pieces of the same shape, one is the other turned or flipped and moved. For the move being tried, this edge is the copy of an edge already known, so it is the same.'
T0685: What it does: two diagonal tiles at a corner are already in one piece. If the other two tiles at that corner were both other pieces, all four edges there would be walls, a cross, which Bricky forbids. So one of the other two joins that piece; when one is already walled off, the other one does.
T0686: See T0685: the solver tries every way to split the four tiles at that corner into pieces without a cross, and keeps the edges that are the same in all of them.
